summary: CLAIM C-0007: The state vs non-state dichotomy is a FALSE DICHOTOMY. Both 'sides' agree suggestions produce real alterations in experience verifiable in brain physiology; the real disagreement is about explanatory necessity/causal role of a 'state' construct — a question of framing more than fact.
content: CLAIM C-0007: The state/non-state dichotomy is increasingly seen as a false or fuzzy dichotomy. Kirsch himself (EV-0003) rejects the uniquely-hypnotic-state idea BUT ALSO rejects compliance-only explanations, affirming suggestions produce 'profound alterations in experience, including dissociative experiences... verified through corresponding changes in brain physiology.' Geagea et al. 2023 (EV-0011): 'broad agreement across theoretical approaches regarding hypnotic analgesia effects, key components, and vocabulary' despite dichotomies. The real disagreement is about the EXPLANATORY NECESSITY and CAUSAL ROLE of a distinct 'state' construct (trance) — i.e., a framing/theory-of-mechanism question — rather than about whether subjective/neural alterations occur (both sides agree they do).
